items.title_found: An explicit lower bound for the unit distance problem
items.meta_description: Abstract page for arXiv paper 2605.20579: An explicit lower bound for the unit distance problem
passages: This improves on very recent work of a team at OpenAI, who proved the same result with an inexplicit exponent greater than $1$, drastically improving on the best previous lower bound and disproving a conjecture of Erdős.
We show that there are sets of $n$ points in the plane with $n$ arbitrarily large that contain more than $n^{1.014}$ pairs of points separated by a distance exactly $1$.
The method is number-theoretic, relying on constructing algebraic number fields of large degree and small discriminant with many primes of small norm via a Golod-Shafarevich criterion argument.
